races.name: Napoleons Casino Hull Dine In Style From £35 EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Connexin Ultrafast Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Fozzie
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's 3yo has solid placed form on Good ground over 7-10f but is a genuine hold-up horse nudged into a midfield mapping here because several true closers contest this race; Fozzie's best racing style requires room from the rear, and racing more prominently than natural may compromise its finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Glen Nevis
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston runner with just two starts, placed on both, and both over distances suggesting this 7½f trip could suit; lightly raced profile means a fitness edge is uncertain after 22 days off, but the form includes a solid second on Good ground that makes this Going no concern.

runners_data.name: Indefensible
runners_data.note: Ollie Pears 3yo who has shown a tendency to race prominently and ran a notable second on Good ground over 7f; this is the only confirmed prominent-style runner to press Bee Farmer, and how aggressively Indefensible challenges early will significantly shape the pace of this race.

runners_data.name: Wats On Tiger
runners_data.note: A 4yo for Brian Rothwell with going listed as UNKNOWN and no race date showing — entirely unexposed in this context and must be treated with maximum caution; the 142lb weight relative to rivals is notable, and without going or form evidence this runner is an unknown quantity in the pace map.

runners_data.name: Bee Farmer
runners_data.note: PJ McDonald rides this confirmed front-runner for Edward Bethell who has found the front on both starts; placed over 8f on Good ground is encouraging for the trip, and with no rival likely to dispute for the lead, the big question is whether this horse can sustain its advantage up the Beverley straight.

runners_data.name: Elias Escape
runners_data.note: Richard & Fahey 3yo who has raced from hold-up on both starts without troubling the judge on Good ground; 31 days since last run is manageable, and with no placed form yet, needs to find meaningful improvement here to figure in the finish.

runners_data.name: Lorca's Waltz
runners_data.note: William Haggas horse returning from a lengthy 150-day absence, with both runs on Standard Tapeta rather than turf; the switch to Good turf is a significant unknown, but the trainer's ability to have horses ready after a break means the layoff alone is not disqualifying — the going and surface shift are the primary concerns.

runners_data.name: Race To The Edge
runners_data.note: Roger Varian 3yo with a third on Good ground over 7f representing the best of its form; returned 10 days ago, lightly raced and unexposed, but the U-style tag means its actual tactical position in running is uncertain, and Varian's operation gives the horse a quality platform.

runners_data.name: Melting Snow
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's hold-up runner has a fifth on Standard and an eighth on Good ground — modest profile to date — and returns after 35 days; needs the pace to be honest to bring its closing style into play, but without any placed form there is little evidence yet that it can execute a winning run from the rear.

races.paceDynamic: Bee Farmer is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival likely to push them for the lead, should be able to dictate a measured, sustainable gallop on Good ground over this 7½f Beverley trip. Indefensible is the only prominent-type racer in the field and is unlikely to cause Bee Farmer serious early grief, meaning the pace is set from one source without meaningful pressure. The hold-up contingent — Fozzie, Elias Escape, Lorca's Waltz, and Melting Snow — will all be racing from behind, but Fozzie has been redistributed to midfield in this map because the field holds more hold-up types than the rear of the race can naturally accommodate; in reality, Fozzie is a true hold-up horse forced into a positional compromise. A controlled, single-source gallop on Good turf over a distance that suits patient, stayer-bred types gives a clear tactical edge to genuine closers with the ability to produce sustained late runs — hold-up horses who can travel smoothly and pick off the leader in the final two furlongs are best placed, provided the pace is honest enough to stretch the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bee Farmer Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Bee Farmer secures an uncontested lead and sets a measured but fair gallop that stretches the field without burning out.
scenarios.body: If Bee Farmer secures an uncontested lead and sets a measured but fair gallop that stretches the field without burning out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves just honest enough to expose Bee Farmer in the final furlong as the hold-up horses produce sustained late runs.
scenarios.body: If the pace proves just honest enough to expose Bee Farmer in the final furlong as the hold-up horses produce sustained late runs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Indefensible tracks Bee Farmer closely and the gallop is slow enough that prominent positions prove decisive.
scenarios.body: If Indefensible tracks Bee Farmer closely and the gallop is slow enough that prominent positions prove decisive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unknown Quantity Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly raced or returning horses — Wats On Tiger, Race To The Edge, or Lorca's Waltz — produces an unexpectedly improved performance that the market has underestimated.
scenarios.body: If one of the lightly raced or returning horses — Wats On Tiger, Race To The Edge, or Lorca's Waltz — produces an unexpectedly improved performance that the market has underestimated.

watchPoints.text: Bee Farmer — watch whether PJ McDonald allows this horse to stride on freely or tries to restrain; if the fractions through the first half mile are particularly slow, the advantage of the front position evaporates and the hold-up horses are handed the race.

Lorca's Waltz — William Haggas horses returning from 150 days off frequently run well first time back, and the booking of Harry Davies is a positive; watch in the market for any significant support as a signal the stable is confident.

Indefensible — the only prominent-style runner capable of pressuring Bee Farmer; if Harry Russell sends this horse forward to challenge for the lead early, the pace dynamic shifts materially and the scenario probabilities change in favour of hold-up horses finishing strongly.

Fozzie — mapped to midfield but a natural hold-up horse; watch how Shane Gray deploys it — if trapped wide or forced to race closer than ideal, the redistribution concern becomes a real factor suppressing its chance.

Wats On Tiger — complete unknown with no going record and an absent last-run date; watch for any pre-race market moves or visible fitness signals as the only available read on this runner's likely impact on the race shape.

races.name: Biffa North Handicap

runners_data.name: Bantz
runners_data.note: Returned to form on Good ground (sim-going 6/15, 1W3P) but is a genuine hold-up horse working against himself in a race where the rear of the field is congested; PJ McDonald keeps him competitive but a clear run from the back is far from guaranteed.

runners_data.name: I Can Boogy
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner for Nigel Tinkler who has placed at this trip on Standard and has a sim-going record of 9/15 (1W1P); a 30-day break and a 0/24 trainer 14-day strike rate temper expectations, but her natural position close to the pace is an asset here.

runners_data.name: Billyjoegold
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr runner with a flagged finishing fade, a genuine hold-up type being squeezed into a midfield slot by the weight of closers in this field; the Standard-ground bias in his recent history and that fading pattern make him hard to trust on this Good surface.

runners_data.name: Summer Rain
runners_data.note: Has run entirely on Standard and Soft in recent appearances with zero wins or places on similar going (0W0P sim-going 3/11), a natural hold-up horse finding his positional preference already occupied; the trainer Lidster has had no winners in 14 days and there is little here to recommend.

runners_data.name: Indy's Angel
runners_data.note: Wears a hood (hg:p) and has been held-up consistently in nine recent starts, making the redistribution to a midfield slot a meaningful departure from her natural race pattern; her sim-going record of 9/15 shows she handles Good ground but 0W1P conversion is modest.

runners_data.name: Miss Willows
runners_data.note: The most recent winner in the field (1/7f Soft, 13 days ago) for Simon Whitaker; a genuine hold-up operator whose best sim-going record (10/15, 1W1P) covers Good, and while she is stepping up in weights (138lbs), the form is live and fresh.

runners_data.name: Emerald Army
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner for Ruth Carr with four places from five runs on Good ground (sim-going 9/15, 0W4P); STYLE_FIT tag signals she is slightly out of her optimal role but uncontested lead control offsets that concern significantly.

runners_data.name: Oselton
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a win and a place on Standard and Soft but only 0W0P from four runs on similar going (sim-going 4/15); Craig Lidster's 0/14 recent trainer form is a negative, though the horse has placed from off the pace at this trip (1/7f STA).

runners_data.name: Valsharah
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's active yard (2/14, hg:t) is a positive angle, and her sim-going record of 5/15 includes a place on Good; a natural hold-up type squeezed into midfield by the density of closers, her best chance requires a pace collapse that the race shape makes unlikely.

runners_data.name: Langholm
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old veteran wearing a hood and cheekpieces (hg:tp) who has run well in Good-ground handicaps historically (sim-going 8/15, 1W4P) but his recent form reads 50-008 and Michael Dods' 3/30 trainer rate is underwhelming; another genuine hold-up horse displaced from his ideal position.

runners_data.name: Elettaria
runners_data.note: John Wainwright has had 3 winners in 7 days which is a minor positive angle, and the 7-year-old's sim-going record of 8/15 (0W1P) shows she handles Good turf; wears a hood (hg:p), a true hold-up performer whose positional squeeze makes finding clear air in a 14-runner field difficult.

runners_data.name: Hear The Drums
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old with a finishing fade flag and a record of 0W0P from five runs on similar going (sim-going 5/7); Fahey's yard is in decent form (5/57) but this horse's tendency to empty late on Good ground undermines his chance from a hold-up position.

runners_data.name: Crystal Aurora
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's 3-year-old has one place from four Good-ground runs (sim-going 4/8) and is a hold-up type dropping back slightly in company; no major red flags but no major positives either, and Robbie Downey will need a truly fast-finishing race that the pace shape does not encourage.

runners_data.name: Lope Y Linda
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good ground 11 days ago (1/7f GOO) for the powerful Tim Easterby yard (5/91) with an apprentice claiming 7lbs; a naturally prominent racer who should slot in just off Emerald Army's shoulder, making her one of the best-placed horses in the race given the anticipated pace shape.

races.paceDynamic: Emerald Army is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in this 14-runner field, will dictate from the front at a sustainable gallop on Good ground over 7½f at Beverley. Lope Y Linda and I Can Boogy are the only other horses with prominent tendencies likely to sit close enough to matter, giving Emerald Army a relatively uncontested lead with a small group tracking. The overwhelming bulk of the field — Bantz, Valsharah, Summer Rain, Indy's Angel, Langholm, Elettaria and others — are natural hold-up types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because there are simply too many closers for all to find their natural rear position; of these, Valsharah and Lope Y Linda are best placed to secure a genuine tracking spot. With a single, uncontested pace-setter controlling fractions on Good turf, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can press Emerald Army or sit just off the pace through the turn, as the steady gallop is unlikely to generate enough momentum for late closers to make significant ground from deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Emerald Army Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Emerald Army goes straight to the front and is allowed to bowl along at a measured, uncontested pace with Lope Y Linda and I Can Boogy just off the shoulder.
scenarios.body: If Emerald Army goes straight to the front and is allowed to bowl along at a measured, uncontested pace with Lope Y Linda and I Can Boogy just off the shoulder.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Lope Y Linda or I Can Boogy press the pace aggressively and run Emerald Army out of it in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Lope Y Linda or I Can Boogy press the pace aggressively and run Emerald Army out of it in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Held-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely false and collapses in the final quarter-mile, creating a rare opportunity for the redistributed hold-up types to close.
scenarios.body: If the pace proves genuinely false and collapses in the final quarter-mile, creating a rare opportunity for the redistributed hold-up types to close.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Handicapper Chaos, No Clear Winner
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses clash for the lead early, the pace becomes ragged and the race degenerates into a gruelling stamina test.
scenarios.body: If multiple horses clash for the lead early, the pace becomes ragged and the race degenerates into a gruelling stamina test.

watchPoints.text: Emerald Army — monitor her early to confirm she goes straight to the front unchallenged; if Lope Y Linda pushes up aggressively, the pace shape changes and the whole race dynamic shifts.
Lope Y Linda — Jake Dickson's 7lb claim makes her competitive on weight and her recent 7f Good-ground win is directly relevant; watch for her pressing Emerald Army into a faster-than-expected gallop.

Valsharah — Michael Appleby's yard is in form and she wears headgear (hg:t), but she needs a clear run from a congested midfield in a race that is likely to be run at a steady pace; any interference leaving the turn will end her chance.

Miss Willows — the only runner in the field with a win in the last fortnight and races fresh well; watch for Tom Eaves to produce her later than ideal, as she will need the pace to collapse slightly to make her hold-up run count.

Hear The Drums and Billyjoegold both carry finishing-fade flags — if either is seen travelling strongly at the two-furlong pole it is likely to be misleading; their recorded tendency to empty late is a caution against reading their mid-race positions as bullish signals.

races.name: Coachman Caravans Classic Handicap

runners_data.name: Keldeo
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner who gets a clean uncontested lead; Good ground suits (10/15 sim-going), won over 6f Good last time, but styled as P with STYLE_FIT flag suggesting a slight question over whether he fully commands from the front over 5f with no pressure.|

runners_data.name: Miss Brazen
runners_data.note: Strong 5f Good-ground handler (14/15 sim-going, 1W over course conditions) for the Easterby yard in form at T14 3/34; a true hold-up horse who will sit last or nearly last and needs a pace collapse that this race shape may not deliver.|

runners_data.name: Fierce
runners_data.note: Finished second on last run and third on Good; genuine hold-up type for Paul Midgley with Tom Eaves up, but only 5/15 on similar going — needs the front to tire which is less likely in this scenario.|

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Applause
runners_data.note: 211-day absence is a significant concern for any each-way interest; all five recent runs came on Standard ground rather than Good (0W on sim-going), making this return to turf on Good an unknown quantity despite a previous win.|

runners_data.name: Ay Gee Ell
runners_data.note: Ay Gee Ell wears a tongue-tie and visor and is a confirmed hold-up horse; mapped into midfield here because the field is saturated with closers, meaning this 4yo will race away from his preferred position and the STYLE_FIT flag tempers expectations.|

runners_data.name: Jojo Rabbit
runners_data.note: Veteran 8yo for Ruth Carr who naturally wants to come from off the pace; Sullivan takes the ride but with the rear crowded, this horse is forced into a midfield slot it does not naturally occupy — the redistribution materially weakens its finishing position.|

runners_data.name: Azuinthejungle
runners_data.note: 4yo prominent racer for Nigel Tinkler, ridden by Faye McManoman; holds a win on Good over 5f and should be able to travel close to Keldeo throughout — one of the more naturally suited runners to this race shape.|

runners_data.name: Lord Abama
runners_data.note: Drops to 5f from a recent run of 6f trips and holds a tongue-tie and visor combination; another true hold-up horse nudged into a midfield mapping — the step down in trip adds further doubt alongside the positional compromise.|

runners_data.name: Dream Deal
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 7yo wears a tongue-strap and blinkers, and has all five recent runs over 6f rather than today's 5f — the trip shortening is a genuine concern. A natural hold-up horse operating out of position in a crowded rear.|

runners_data.name: Bibendum
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing 5yo for Julie Camacho with the visor retained; only 5/15 on sim-going but has 5f turf form and should be able to sit just behind Keldeo in second position, making this one of the better-placed prominent types in the field.|

races.paceDynamic: Keldeo is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will stride into an uncontested position and control tempo from the outset on Good ground at Beverley. Azuinthejungle and Bibendum will push up to prominent positions just behind, but neither has the profile to seriously harass Keldeo for the lead, meaning the pace is likely to be honest but not frenetic — a sustainable gallop that keeps the race honest without blowing up. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the track map can accommodate at the rear; Ay Gee Ell, Jojo Rabbit, Lord Abama and Dream Deal are all true hold-up horses who will be forced wider and less ideally placed than they would naturally prefer, compromising their late-run potential. This race shape — a single front-runner controlling a moderate, uncontested tempo — firmly favours horses who can race prominently and travel with cover, rather than pure closers who need a pace collapse that is unlikely to materialise.

scenarios.title: Keldeo Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Keldeo is allowed to stride clear from the gates and dictates a sustainable, uncontested tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: If Keldeo is allowed to stride clear from the gates and dictates a sustainable, uncontested tempo throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If Keldeo's lead is pegged back in the final furlong by a prominent challenger who has tracked him economically throughout.
scenarios.body: If Keldeo's lead is pegged back in the final furlong by a prominent challenger who has tracked him economically throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected and Keldeo ties up in the final furlong, opening the door for a hold-up horse to finish with purpose.
scenarios.body: If the pace is faster than expected and Keldeo ties up in the final furlong, opening the door for a hold-up horse to finish with purpose.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If crowding or a slow early break disrupts the field's order and creates a stop-start pace that scrambles the race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: If crowding or a slow early break disrupts the field's order and creates a stop-start pace that scrambles the race shape entirely.

watchPoints.text: Keldeo is the only horse confirmed for the lead — if he misses the break or is slow away, the entire race shape collapses and the field becomes a scramble with no natural pace-setter.|

The rear is packed with redistributed hold-up horses (Ay Gee Ell, Jojo Rabbit, Lord Abama, Dream Deal) — watch for traffic issues and crowding from 2f out as they all try to find a run simultaneously.|

Spirit Of Applause returns after 211 days off and has no recent Good-ground form — if it strips fitter than expected the Tim Easterby yard have previous form getting horses ready first time up, but it remains a significant fitness risk.|
Azuinthejungle and Bibendum will contest second and third early on — whichever settles better and tracks Keldeo most economically in the first two furlongs is the one to follow into the straight.|

races.name: Churchill Tyres Handicap

runners_data.name: Can I Kiss You
runners_data.note: Recent form at 8f on Good is inconsistent (8-2-8 in last three similar-going runs), Tom Eaves up for a yard without a strike in 14 days; genuine hold-up type who will be racing in a more forward position than suits, tempering confidence in a finishing burst.

runners_data.name: Copper And Five
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr yard shows 1 winner from 27 in 14 days and this veteran of 10 has a solid record at 8f on Good (10 runs, 1W 2P); a true closer whose redistribution to midfield compresses his natural patient style, though his consistency and good-ground record make him a player in a sprint finish.

runners_data.name: Anificas Beauty
runners_data.note: Holds a win at 8f on Good and has shown ability to finish strongly, but recent starts at 12f on Soft and sprint trips on Standard suggest trip/going mix is unsettled; displaces naturally to midfield rather than the rear, which may actually suit if the race becomes a driving finish.

runners_data.name: Hostelry
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with two wins and five places from 10 similar-going starts, making him the most course-and-conditions proven runner in the field; Tom Kiely-Marshall (5) takes the ride for the same Carr yard, and as a hold-up type with tactical nous he holds the best realistic claim to drift forward and at least set a modest tempo.

runners_data.name: Wicklow Way
runners_data.note: Won last time at 10f on Standard and has course experience, but form on Good going is limited (0W 0P from seven similar runs); Cam Hardie in the saddle and a slightly fresher profile at 14 days could see him edge forward into a lead role that no one else wants, though good-ground form is the key question.

runners_data.name: Little Ted
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby sends this nine-year-old out in a visor, and the yard is active (5/91 in 14 days); placed three times at 8f on Good but has not won in this going band, and redistribution to midfield means Warren Fentiman (3) will need to find gaps in a tightly bunched field.

runners_data.name: Rogers Dream
runners_data.note: Gihan Arnolda yard without a win in five 14-day runners; limited form evidence on Good going (3 runs, 0W 0P) and a disqualification in recent form adds uncertainty; William Carson is an asset but this horse's redistribution from the rear leaves it with few clear tactical advantages in a sprint finish.

runners_data.name: Mavetheforcebewivu
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and has one placing from nine Good-going starts — P J McDonald is the obvious positive, and the yard fires one from 12 in 14 days; naturally a hold-up type who will be crowded into the midfield pack, and without the stamina profile to grind through a genuine test this looks difficult at the OR of 46.

races.paceDynamic: This is an unusual 1m½f Beverley handicap with all eight runners classified as hold-up types, meaning no confirmed front-runner will take command from the gates — the field will likely crawl into the first bend before accelerating only in the straight, compressing the race into a sprint finish from the home turn. Hostelry and Wicklow Way, though mapped as hold-up, have the best claims to drift forward and establish some early tempo, but neither is a natural pace-setter and any gallop they create will be modest at best. The field holds significantly more genuine hold-up horses than can all occupy their natural rear positions — Can I Kiss You, Copper And Five, Anificas Beauty, Little Ted, Rogers Dream, and Mavetheforcebewivu are all true closers who will be shuffled into a congested midfield pack, stripping them of their preferred tactical setup. This shape strongly favours whichever runner can produce the most powerful late surge from the widest position in an end-to-end sprint, with course experience and a horse that stays every yard of this stiff 1m½f test holding a marginal edge.

scenarios.title: Sprint Finish, No Pace

scenarios.body: If the field idles through the early stages and the race erupts into a flat-out dash from the home turn.

scenarios.title: Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If a fraction of genuine pace allows the true hold-up types to find their rhythm and pounce from off the back.
scenarios.body: If a fraction of genuine pace allows the true hold-up types to find their rhythm and pounce from off the back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Horse Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one runner breaks clear of the tactical crawl and builds an uncontested lead that the field cannot close down.
scenarios.body: If one runner breaks clear of the tactical crawl and builds an uncontested lead that the field cannot close down.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide-Draw Flier
scenarios.trigger: If a high-drawn runner exploits the lack of early pace to ease across and steal a prominent rail position in the absence of any challenge.
scenarios.body: If a high-drawn runner exploits the lack of early pace to ease across and steal a prominent rail position in the absence of any challenge.

watchPoints.text: Hostelry is the most likely horse to drift forward and control a modest pace — if Tom Kiely-Marshall (5) can establish a handy position on the rail, he becomes a significant threat in the absence of any confirmed front-runner.

Wicklow Way's trainer Mark Walford has one winner from 19 in 14 days and Cam Hardie could attempt to steal a soft lead — watch the opening furlong to see whether this four-year-old breaks sharply and exploits the pace vacuum.

Copper And Five has the best good-going record in the field across 15 similar runs; if the race compresses into a sprint finish as expected, James Sullivan's positioning from the early stages will be the key factor to monitor.

With six of eight runners tagged as redistributed hold-up types, the field faces serious congestion through the first bend at Beverley — watch for crowding and interference as runners jostle for position in the absence of any dominant pace-setting horse.

Little Ted's visor and Mavetheforcebewivu's visor suggest connections are trying to generate more early enthusiasm from both horses — if either breaks smartly and shows unexpected pace, the entire race shape changes.

races.name: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Hull Handicap

runners_data.name: Pisanello
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator trained by David O'Meara with P J McDonald in the saddle — form figures of 4th and 5th on Good ground at around this trip give moderate hope, but seven wins from 135 career starts flags a horse that finds little when asked and consistent placing at OR 55 suggests a lower ceiling now.|

runners_data.name: Daring Leader
runners_data.note: Won twice at 10f on Tapeta before a 30-day break, and three of his last five runs have been placed at this distance; Harry Russell is an inexperienced conditional but the horse's consistent hold-up form on Good ground and a fresh return make him one of the more interesting non-front-runners.|

runners_data.name: Quirke On Parole
runners_data.note: Placed twice at 10f on Good in recent history and arrives 30 days fresh under Cam Hardie; the 4-year-old has shown enough at this trip to be considered but his last three runs have all been mid-to-rear finishes and the modest pace may not bring him into the race until too late.|

runners_data.name: Inspiring Speeches
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed pace-setter and likely to lead unchallenged, having won twice on Good ground at 10-12f; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) is noted but here she is actually racing in her natural forward role, so that discount does not apply — the concern is whether her recent 5th and 9th suggest declining form.|

runners_data.name: Hijo De La Luna
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won at 10f on Tapeta 12 days ago and returns quickly; the visor is a key headgear flag suggesting a horse that needs to be held together, and his Good-ground record at 12f (4th in latest) gives confidence he will stay on — most likely to take the fight to Inspiring Speeches.|

runners_data.name: Dandy's Angel
runners_data.note: Trainer John Wainwright in good form at 3/7 over 14 days and returning after just 12 days; this 9-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by nature but the overcrowded rear means he is unlikely to get his preferred position — the age and poor recent form figures (0,3,8,9,5) make improvement hard to project.|

runners_data.name: Sassy Glory
runners_data.note: Mark Walford's second string alongside Quirke On Parole, prominent in style and wearing a hood; recent form of 9th on Good at 12f is unpromising, and while she has placed at shorter trips on better surfaces, this distance on turf has not brought out her best.|

runners_data.name: Regal Glory
runners_data.note: Roger Fell sends this 6-year-old out 20 days after a run, and the trainer has 3 winners from 11 over 14 days — a mild positive; however, the horse is a genuine back-of-the-field type forced into a midfield slot by the congested field shape, and four consecutive non-winning runs at 12-16f suggest the uphill finish will expose limitations.|

runners_data.name: Sweet Cicely
runners_data.note: Form figures of 0,0,0 in the last three outings make this a very hard case on current ability; a genuine deep hold-up runner who is unlikely to find a true pace to chase at Beverley, and Mike Sowersby's stable is quiet at T14 0/6 — the blinkers flag some concern.|

runners_data.name: Rajawail
runners_data.note: Twelve of his last 15 runs have been at this distance on Good ground yet he has never won in those conditions — the form profile is one of repeated near-misses that never materialise; a tail-bandaged hold-up horse mapped into midfield, he needs a stronger pace than this race is likely to generate.|

runners_data.name: Pureis King
runners_data.note: Faye Bramley's 4-year-old carries a prominent ⚠ fade flag backed by form figures of 8,8,8 in recent runs; a natural hold-up type placed into midfield, the combination of a stamina concern at this trip, 49 days off, and a stable running at T14 3/6 without a convincing record makes this a speculative proposition.|

races.paceDynamic: Inspiring Speeches is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 1m2f handicap and, with no genuine rival pressing for the lead, is expected to bowl along at a sustainable, controlled gallop on Good ground at Beverley. Hijo De La Luna and Sassy Glory are the likely nearest pursuers from a prominent position, sitting just behind the pace as Inspiring Speeches dictates terms around the turning track. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than can realistically race at the rear — Pureis King, Dandy's Angel, Sweet Cicely, Regal Glory and Rajawail are all true hold-up horses who have been redistributed into midfield on the map simply because natural back-of-the-field spots are over-subscribed; Inspiring Speeches and Hijo De La Luna are most likely to actually secure their forward positions. With one relaxed pace-setter, a Good surface, and Beverley's uphill finish rewarding those who travel economically, this race shape strongly favours horses that can race prominently or in a handy midfield position and sustain their effort — pure hold-up finishers dependent on a strong pace to chase down will find conditions less than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Inspiring Speeches Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Inspiring Speeches secures a clear lead and is allowed to control the tempo without harassment from Hijo De La Luna or Sassy Glory.

scenarios.body: If Hijo De La Luna and Sassy Glory press Inspiring Speeches enough to set up a sustained duel that cuts down the pace-setter late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Handy Midfield Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs and a well-positioned midfield horse with strong form at the trip swoops late.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs and a well-positioned midfield horse with strong form at the trip swoops late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce From Deep
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to bring the true hold-up horses — Pureis King, Sweet Cicely, Rajawail — into play from their natural rear positions.

watchPoints.text: Inspiring Speeches — watch whether Tom Kiely-Marshall (5lb claimer) allows the horse to stride on uncontested or gets hustled; if she bowls along in front on her own terms the race could be over a long way out.

Hijo De La Luna — equipped with a visor and returning quickly after a win, watch his early behaviour in the stalls and whether Aiden Brookes tracks Inspiring Speeches closely; if he sits just off the pace rather than chasing hard, he becomes a serious winning threat.

Daring Leader — off 30 days and dropping back to turf from Tapeta, watch his pre-race market moves; Harry Russell's conditional claim is valuable and if the horse settles well from his hold-up position he could produce a sustained run up Beverley's climb.

Dandy's Angel and Pureis King — both are genuine hold-up horses squeezed into midfield by the redistribution effect; watch early to see if either drifts back to their natural rear position, which would effectively remove them from contention given the anticipated moderate pace.

Rajawail — despite strong course-and-distance statistics on paper, his zero wins in 12 qualifying runs is a red flag; watch for him to race prominently despite his hold-up profile, which would signal the rider is departing from form entirely.
